hints.title: Turn the mixing ratio into convenient amounts
hints.body: Use 12 units of P, 5 units of Q and 3 units of R. The mixture then has 20 units altogether. Let r be the fraction of R that is red.
hints.recap: A ratio gives relative quantities, so you may choose convenient amounts with that ratio.
hints.pitfall: The three paints contribute different amounts; their red percentages cannot be averaged equally.
hints.pause: Find the red amount supplied by P and by Q.

recall.reminder: A ratio gives relative quantities, so you may choose convenient amounts with that ratio.

hints.title: Conserve the red paint
hints.body: The amount of red paint in any portion is its volume multiplied by its red fraction. The three red amounts must add to the red amount in the final mixture.
hints.recap: Translate each concentration into an amount before balancing the mixture.
hints.pitfall: The unknown red fraction belongs to R, so its denominator is the volume of R.
hints.pause: Form the red-amount equation, solve for the red fraction of R and convert it to a percentage.

recall.reminder: Translate each concentration into an amount before balancing the mixture.

solution:
1. Choose amounts matching the ratio. Take volumes 12, 5 and 3, totalling 20. Let r be the red fraction of R.

2. Conserve the red amount. 12×310+5×15+3r=20×14. Thus 185+1+3r=5, giving 3r=25.

3. Divide by the volume of R. r=215, so the percentage is 100×215=403%=1313%.

Answer C. The weighted red amounts, rather than the bare percentages, must add.
